subject.title: [Feature]: Add runtime testing for skill workshop proposals before apply

question: What pre-apply execution boundary should Skill Workshop support for runtime-testing pending proposals before they can be applied?
rationale: The useful behavior requires a human choice about whether OpenClaw may execute or simulate unapproved generated skill content, what side effects are allowed, and whether failures block apply or only annotate proposal health.

options.title: Staged load/schema MVP
options.body: Add proposal load, discovery, and schema validation first, record skipped invocation status, and defer side-effecting invocation until a test-case/sandbox contract exists.

options.title: Full sandboxed invocation contract
options.body: Design proposal-provided or generated test cases plus explicit filesystem, network, tool-policy, and side-effect isolation before wiring invocation into CLI, Gateway, and agent flows.

options.title: Keep manual runtime testing
options.body: Leave Skill Workshop apply gated by static scan and human review only, and document that runtime behavior remains an operator proof step for now.

recommendation.title: Staged load/schema MVP
recommendation.body: Add proposal load, discovery, and schema validation first, record skipped invocation status, and defer side-effecting invocation until a test-case/sandbox contract exists.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle authored the merged Skill Workshop service, CLI, and Gateway introduction that this validation contract would extend.
